From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@aperturehealth.com>, Mike Connelly <mike.connelly@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP Timeline & Legal Handoff — Aperture pilot fast-lane sequencing

Hi Elena / Mike —

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. As discussed, I put together a concise Mutual Action Plan (attached) that maps the evaluation milestones to the legal / procurement gating items so we can keep the pilot on a tight timeline. High level ask: can Aperture confirm the procurement sign-off owner and whether your legal team is prepared to review our MSA v3 with the redlines attached by end of next week?

Key milestones in the attached MAP (high-level):
- Week 1: Security questionnaire + infra checklist (we've pre-filled most responses) — Aperture to return by 10/26
- Week 2: Legal review of MSA v3 redlines — target 11/02 for initial comments
- Week 3: Order form negotiation and PO submission — target 11/09
- Week 4: Signed MSA/DPA + Order form = go-live scheduling

Open items for you:
1) Procurement contact and PO cadence (who routes POs internally?)
2) Any mandatory legal clauses (insurance, data residency) we should pre-acknowledge before your legal review?
3) Confirmation that SOC2 report request can be fulfilled with our compliance package (we've attached Security_Responses_Aperture.docx).

I'll loop Laura (contracts) and Jonas (customer success) to help coordinate the legal handoff and scheduling. If it helps, we can run a 30-minute legal prep call tomorrow to walk your counsel through the redlines and where we expect fast agreement.

Next step: Elena, could you confirm procurement owner and a preferred time for the prep call?

Thanks —
Marcus

Date: 2026-10-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP Timeline & Legal Handoff — Aperture pilot fast-lane sequencing

Marcus —

Appreciate the MAP and the pre-filled security responses — that helps a lot. Quick answers:
- Procurement owner for this engagement is Mike Connelly (cc'd) — he owns PO routing and budget clearance.
- Our legal lead (Sasha Martin) is available for a 30-min prep call tomorrow at 2pm PT; I'll introduce her on the call so your contracts team can go through the redlines.
- Data residency: Aperture requires EU data to remain in EU regions for PHI-adjacent workloads; for this pilot we'll be using US-region infra but will want an explicit clause placeholder in the DPA.

We will review the security doc internally; one ask up front — can Redwood provide a copy of the SOC2 Type II cover letter and the latest penetration test summary? That will speed our infosec sign-off.

I confirmed with Procurement that a standard PO route is possible but final PO requires signed MSA + order form; Procurement can provision a preliminary commitment letter if legal confirms timing.

Elena
Elena Park | Dir. of Product Strategy, Aperture Health
elena.park@aperturehealth.com | +1 212-555-1208

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@aperturehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-23T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP Timeline & Legal Handoff — Aperture pilot fast-lane sequencing

Hi Elena / Marcus —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Quick notes from contracts:
- We'll join the 2pm PT call and walk through the MSA redlines (Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf). To be efficient, I've highlighted three negotiation buckets in the doc: indemnity cap mechanics, data processing/geography language, and termination/rollback for pilot data.
- On data residency: we can add a DPA placeholder clause to the order form that specifies regional controls for PHI-adjacent processing. That will be a conditional clause until the pilot scope is finalized.
- SOC2 / PT artifacts: I'll upload the cover letter and a redacted pentest summary to the Drive link now (link in thread metadata). We redact IP-specific findings but include remediation posture.

Process suggestion (to keep your timeline):
1) 10/23: Legal prep call (2pm PT) — walk redlines and agree on 1-2 concession points ready for PO
2) 10/26: Aperture returns completed security checklist + confirmation of PO intent
3) 11/02: Aperture legal provides inline comments on MSA v3; Redwood responds within 48 hours
4) 11/09: Order form finalized + procurement issues PO (target)

Jonas and Marissa will be the points for onboarding/runbook items once the contract is in place — we'll prepare a minimal statement of work and a go-live window that matches the PO.

If anything in the redlines is non-starter for Aperture, call it out during the prep call and we'll mark those for escalation.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

From: Mike Connelly <mike.connelly@aperturehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@aperturehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-26T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP Timeline & Legal Handoff — Aperture pilot fast-lane sequencing

Marcus / Laura —

Thanks for the call earlier today — was helpful to see the redlines laid out. Procurement confirms we can issue a preliminary commitment letter by 10/29 contingent on the following:
- Receipt of SOC2 cover letter and redacted pentest summary (please upload to shared Drive by EOD 10/27)
- Agreement on the DPA placeholder language that matches our PHI-adjacent requirement (we'll circulate suggested phrasing post-call)

Assuming those two items land on the dates above, Procurement will prioritize the PO and expects to issue a PO by 11/09 as discussed. Once we have the PO, legal will execute the MSA and we can book the go-live window.

I'll follow up with the suggested DPA wording from our counsel tomorrow.

Mike Connelly
Sr. Manager, Procurement — Aperture Health
